test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 04 May 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'Option 1'** i.e. **'Received'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In this context, the past tense** "received" **is appropriate because the sentence is discussing an event in the past- The project's gaining of support from American and Russian government officials.
 
• **"Received"** means to have been given or presented with something.

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is: *'The "Sesame Street" spinoff set out to be the first Russian-language educational TV program aimed specifically at preschoolers. The project** received **support form both American and Russian government officials. "If we do not reform our (4) ______, we can hardly hope that we will reform our society, " (5) ______ Elena Lenskaya, a director in Russia's Ministry of Education, during a 1992 U.S. congressional hearing on the planned adaptation.'*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's look at why the other options don't fit as well:
 
 
• **"Did received"** - This is incorrect because in English, when we use "did" for emphasis or to form a question, the main verb should be in its base form, so the correct form would be "did receive". However, in this context, just "received" fits better.
 
• **"Receiving"** - This is the present participle form of "receive" and would be used in continuous tenses. However, the context here is talking about a completed action in the past, so the simple past "received" fits better.
 
• **"Receive"** - This is the base form of the verb and would generally be used in present simple tense or imperative sentences. In this context, where a past action is being described, the past tense "received" is more appropriate.
